newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila sets full oil deregulation in February.
newsitem.headline: Manila sets full oil deregulation in February.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos signed on Tuesday an executive order setting the full deregulation of the domestic oil industry on February 8.
Under earlier plans, the Department of Energy was to implement full deregulation not later than March 1997.

In the executive order, a copy of which was sent to Reuters, Ramos said the energy department had recommended early deregulation due to the likely depletion of the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF) on or about February 7.
The OPSF is a buffer fund that cushions domestic prices from fluctuations in crude prices in the world market and the foreign exchange rate.
Since August 1996 or the start of partial oil industry deregulation, the OPSF had absorbed increases in petroleum products exceeding 50 centavos per litre.
The order added that full oil industry deregulation was possible due to the stable price of crude oil and petroleum products in the world market and the foreign exchange rate.
Crude oil prices had been steady at $21 to $23 a barrel since October 1996 and petroleum product prices were stable since middle of December, the order said.
The order added that the exchange rate of 26.20 peso to the U.S. dollar had been steady for the past 12 months.
